findings.title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is exposed as GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe, and it writes topic_users.notification_level before rendering. Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, and this app predates SameSite cookies, so a logged-in victim can be forced to change topic or PM notification level by an image, link prefetch, or other cross-site GET. The write is also not idempotent: a level above regular becomes regular, and regular becomes muted, so a refresh or a second full page load applies a second transition (watching becomes regular, then muted). The Ember unsubscribe route never performs the change itself, so the only implementation of the action is this GET side effect.

findings.title: Unsubscribe leaves tracking and watching users notified
findings.body: The email string says the link will stop notifications for this topic, and the new page says the user will stop receiving them, but unsubscribe only sets notification_level to muted when it is already regular (1) or lower. Tracking (2) and watching (3) are both written to regular (1). Tracking receives the same reply, mention, and quote emails as regular, so that click changes nothing about email. Watching stops every-post emails but still sends reply, mention, and quote emails. A second request then takes regular to muted, so the first confirmation is false and a refresh changes the result.

findings.title: Raw save does not record an explicit notification choice
findings.body: unsubscribe assigns notification_level and calls save! instead of TopicUser.change. change is what sets notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, and publishes the /topic/:id notification_level_change event. save! leaves the old reason in place. Rows created when an email is sent often have a nil reason, because TopicUser.change is called with only last_emailed_post_number. update_last_read in topic_user.rb then forces notification_level back to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and the auto-track time threshold is met, and auto_track does the same for a nil reason. For those users the unsubscribe does not stick, and already-open clients never get the level-change event.

findings.title: Missing TopicUser row 500s unsubscribe
findings.body: unsubscribe loads TopicUser with find_by(user_id, topic_id) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If there is no row, tu is nil and this raises NoMethodError, so the request 500s and nothing is saved. A topic_users row is not created for every user who can see a topic; the URL is predictable and any logged-in user who can see the topic can open it without having visited or been emailed. TopicUser.change already creates the row when it is missing; this action does not use it.

findings.title: Unsubscribe template does not match its route
findings.body: The router registers a top-level topicUnsubscribe route at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe, and the route, controller, and view are all the topic-unsubscribe module. Ember looks up template topic-unsubscribe, i.e. templates/topic-unsubscribe. The template was added at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which is the name for a nested topic.unsubscribe route that was not registered, and there is no matching topic/unsubscribe controller. After the Rails shell boots, the transition fails with a missing template, so the confirmation text and the notification dropdown never render.

findings.title: Per-topic unsubscribe link is not tied to the recipient
findings.body: Topic#unsubscribe_url is only the public topic URL plus /unsubscribe, and UserNotifications puts that same link in every recipient's mail. TopicsController#unsubscribe is behind ensure_logged_in and always updates current_user, with no signed user or email token. Unlike the existing digest path email/unsubscribe/:key, a logged-out recipient opening the message from a mail client is not unsubscribed by the click. If someone else is logged in (forwarded mail or a shared browser), that account's notification level is changed instead of the recipient's.

findings.title: render :show drops canonical URL on topic pages
findings.body: perform_show_response is also used by TopicsController#show, which calls canonical_url only after perform_show_response returns. Previously the HTML format block did not render, so Rails deferred the template until the action finished and @canonical_url was already set for the layout. The new render :show inside format.html renders the layout immediately, before that call, so every topic HTML response loses its canonical link. Unsubscribe HTML has the same gap because it never sets a canonical URL either.

findings.title: No coverage of unsubscribe behavior or the new link
findings.body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into Email::MessageBuilder so the new unsubscribe_link translation does not raise MissingInterpolationArgument, but the example still only checks that the user-preferences URL appears in the text body. It never asserts that the per-topic unsubscribe URL is present in the text or HTML part, or that List-Unsubscribe changed. There is no controller or request spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe, so the level transition, nil TopicUser crash, slug redirect, and session requirements are untested.
